chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Bukayr ibn Ayn and Burayd and Fudayl and Ismail al-Azraq and Ma'mar ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they said:

When a man divorces [his wife] during the blood of childbirth, or divorces her after he has touched her, then his divorcing her is not a [valid] divorce. And if he divorces her at the commencement of her waiting period, while she is clean from non-coitus, and two just witnesses do not testify to that, then his divorcing her is not a [valid] divorce.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for an invalid divorce in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent chain of Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, establishes the Shia juristic principle that talaq requires specific conditions of purity (tuhr) and sexual abstinence to be valid. It highlights the significance of the 'three divorces' mechanism by defining when a pronouncement fails to count as a binding divorce, thereby protecting the wife's status during the waiting period (iddah). The requirement of two just witnesses underscores the communal verification essential in Shia fiqh to prevent arbitrary dissolution of marriage.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, and Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Bukeyr Bin Ayn, and Bureyd, and Fuzayl, and Ismail Al Azraq, and Ma’mar Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both of them having said:

‘When the man divorces during blood of the childbirth, or divorces her after having touched her, so his divorcing her is not with a (valid) divorce, and if he divorces her during the commencement of her waiting period, (when she is) clean from other than copulation, and two just witnesses did not witness upon that, so his divorcing her is not a (valid) divorce’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Bukayr ibn ’A‘yan and Burayd and Fudayl and ’Isma’il al-Azraq and Mu’ammar ibn Yahya from abu Ja‘far and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, who has said the following: “

When a man during a woman’s experiencing blood discharge because of childbirth or after going to bed with her divorces, such divorce is not a valid divorce. A divorce at such time when commencing waiting period is possible and valid, that it is in a menses-free time but without the presence of two just witnesses, such divorce also is not a valid divorce.’”
